pageCache.text:
An independent day and boarding school for girls and boys aged 11-19.
Welcome from the Head
Welcome to Cobham Hall. Choosing the right school for your child is an important decision, and I am delighted to introduce you to a community where every student is truly known, valued and supported to become the best version of themselves.
At Cobham Hall, we believe education should develop the whole child, preparing them for life beyond school. Through a personalised approach, excellent teaching and outstanding pastoral care, we nurture academic ambition alongside confidence, character, curiosity and independence. Our students are encouraged to discover their strengths, pursue their passions and embrace opportunities beyond the classroom – whether on the stage, the sports field, through adventure or in service to others.
Our unique family feel is truly special, providing students an environment where they can develop a genuine sense of belonging and flourish. Our aim is not simply to prepare students for examinations, but to equip them with the skills, values and self-belief they need to thrive in an ever-changing world.
I warmly invite you to come and see what makes Cobham Hall such a special place to learn, grow and belong. Reach out to us today to visit us for a tour, taster day or open morning and experience all we have to offer first-hand.
Headteacher at Cobham Hall
Inspiring Surroundings
Why choose us?
‘There’s more in you than you think’
We believe untold brilliance lies within each of our students, and that each has the potential to develop skills and abilities they may never have believed possible. Our School motto, ‘There’s more in you than you think,’ underlines this. We are committed to providing our students with the academic knowledge to flourish, and to inspiring each student to have the courage to challenge themselves and find their own path in life.
Happy young people learn, and we place student wellbeing at the heart of everything we do, ensuring trust, respect, honesty, kindness and tolerance infuse every aspect of the educational experience. In our diverse and tolerant environment, students feel safe to question the world around them, to develop their curiosity and creativity, and to discover there is more in them than they know.
A member of the international Round Square network of schools, our core values are built around the Round Square IDEALS of Internationalism, Democracy, Environmentalism, Adventure, Leadership and Service.
Our School Values
Values
Welcome to Bligh House – An Innovation in SEND
We are excited to announce the opening of Bligh House SEND Centre located within the grounds of Cobham Hall School. Bligh House is a new SEND centre catering for students aged 11 to 16 with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
This centre of excellence is the result of a unique collaboration between Mill Hill Education Group, one of the UK’s fastest-growing charitable independent school groups, and Chiltern Way Academy Trust, an outstanding specialist Multi Academy Trust.
Latest News
Discover how our World Challenge 2026 students developed resilience, leadership and teamwork during an unforgettable expedition through Borneo.
Cobham Hall is delighted to welcome Mr Brown as our new Head from September 2026, bringing experience, ambition and a commitment to helping every student thrive.
We are proud to announce Mr Turner’s Kent Education Award win for Secondary School Teacher of the Year in Art, recognising his creativity, leadership and inspiring impact on students.
Part of the Mill Hill Education Group
Our collection of schools spans from London and the surrounding areas to as far as Thailand. With over 250 acres of scenic grounds across all our locations, there is plenty of room for woods, fields, sports pitches and much more, providing pupils with plenty of space to grow. We are proud to offer an outstanding education across all our schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Why Choose Bligh House SEND Centre | Special Educational Needs | Cobham Hall Independent School
pageCache.text:
1. Unrivalled Expertise
Backed by two award-winning institutions, Chiltern Way Academy Trust and Mill Hill Education Group, our therapeutic education program blends the core values of independent schooling with a focus on Emotional Based School Non Attendance (EBSNA). Chiltern Way Academy's proven success in autism education brings a wealth of experience and dedication to every child’s journey.
2. Stunning, Safe Setting
The new facility is located on the magnificent grounds of Cobham Hall School, Kent, with easy access to London. Bligh House offers a serene and spacious environment that enhances wellbeing and learning for all SEND children to thrive. While retaining the beauty and history of this Grade 1 listed building, we have modernised it with state-of-the-art learning resources and support systems to ensure your child has access to the best of both worlds.
3. High Standards of Care and Support
We understand that the needs of children extend beyond the classroom. Our highly trained staff provide exceptional learning support services, ensuring the emotional and physical wellbeing of every child with EBSNA. From small class sizes to expert pastoral care, we address challenges such as school avoidance, by creating a supportive community where every child feels valued and understood.
4. Focus on Independence and Life Skills
We place emphasis on preparing our students for the future, empowering them to lead fulfilling lives. Our curriculum is designed to not only achieve academic success but also to build critical life skills, self-management, and independence including social skills.
5. Exceptional Facilities
Our SEND provision sits as a standalone building next to Cobham Hall School and caters to the diverse needs including autism, mental health disorders and anxiety. Our facilities include sensory rooms, quiet areas, access to Cobham Hall’s swimming pool, sports hall and extensive and peaceful outdoor spaces. Your child will have access to the best resources, enhancing their educational experience.
6. Holistic Support
We believe that education is a partnership between the school and the family. We offer ongoing support to parents and carers, including regular communication, workshops, and an open-door policy that ensures you are always part of your child’s educational journey. We also provide a comprehensive transition process to ensure that every new student feels comfortable and confident from day one.

Our Curriculum
The curriculum at Bligh House is designed to support each child’s individual needs and help them feel confident and ready to learn. The curriculum is designed to fill gaps in learning attributed to time missed from education.
Where children have missed learning, we gently revisit and introduce key knowledge to help them access age-appropriate lessons with confidence. Teachers regularly check understanding and provide support to help fill any gaps.
Alongside academic learning, we place a strong focus on developing social skills, communication, and interaction. Children also benefit from integrated support such as speech and language and occupational therapy within the everyday learning environment.
Our curriculum includes:
Maths, English, Science, PSHE, PE, IT, Humanities, Art, and Food Technology, play skills and PFA (preparation for adulthood)

Celebrating Mr Turner’s Success at the Kent Education Awards
We are proud to share some exciting news from the Cobham Hall community. Our very own Art teacher, Mr Turner, has been named Secondary School Teacher of the Year in Art at the recent Kent Education Awards - a fantastic achievement and truly well-deserved recognition of his dedication, creativity and passion for teaching.
Mr Turner has made an extraordinary impact within the Art Department at Cobham Hall, inspiring students through a teaching approach that is both innovative and deeply student-focused. His lessons encourage creativity, curiosity and self-expression, while also creating a supportive environment where every student feels valued and empowered to succeed.
At the heart of Mr Turner’s teaching is a commitment to helping students develop confidence and resilience. Whether students are discovering Art for the first time or preparing for advanced creative study, he ensures that each individual is encouraged to explore their own ideas, take creative risks and develop their artistic expression. His inclusive and encouraging approach has helped countless students grow not only as artists, but also as confident and independent learners.
“I’m incredibly honoured to receive the Kent Secondary Teacher of the Year award. Creativity has the power to build confidence, resilience and opportunity, and I’m very lucky to work with such talented students and supportive colleagues every day.” — Mr Turner
Under Mr Turner’s leadership, Art at Cobham Hall continues to flourish. Students are inspired to think ambitiously about their futures, with many pursuing pathways into creative industries and university study. His enthusiasm for the subject and genuine investment in student success have made a lasting impression across the School community.
A recent testament to Mr Turner’s inspiring approach can also be seen in the success of our students. Our talented students, Bond, Lia and Grace, were all shortlisted for the John Downton Art Awards and attended the exhibition in February 2026. As one of the largest and most prestigious young artists’ competitions in Kent, the awards celebrate exceptional creative talent from across the county. Being shortlisted is a remarkable achievement, and each student impressed the judges with their originality, technical skill and distinctive artistic voice.
Looking ahead, we are also delighted that from September 2026, Mr Turner will lead our new International Art and Design Foundation Programme in partnership with NCUK. This exciting one-year programme will provide students with the opportunity to explore a broad range of Art and Design disciplines while developing the academic knowledge and practical skills needed for university and future creative careers around the world.
The programme reflects Mr Turner’s personalised and forward-thinking approach to education, giving students the freedom to develop their creativity while preparing for the next stage of their academic and professional journeys. We are excited to see how his leadership and expertise will continue to shape the experiences of aspiring young artists at Cobham Hall.
Congratulations once again to Mr Turner on his outstanding achievement. We are incredibly proud to celebrate this recognition and look forward to seeing the continued positive impact of his work within our School community.

pageCache.pageTitle: World Challenge 2026: Student-Led Expedition to Borneo
pageCache.text:
World Challenge 2026: An Unforgettable Expedition to Borneo
This month, a small group of students embarked on an extraordinary expedition, straight into the wild heart of Borneo as part of the 2026 World Challenge.
From the moment they arrived in Kota Kinabalu, the students were in control of their adventure with each student taking on a leadership role from Day Boss, Safety Officer, Accountant, Wellbeing Lead, Photographer and Food Coordinator. Working together, they managed daily budgets, planned meals, coordinated with the local ground crew, organised drink breaks and looked after one another's wellbeing.
The expedition began with an introduction to the rich history and culture of Sabah. Students explored Kota Kinabalu, learning about the region's fascinating past, from its heritage to the lasting impact of British colonial rule. They embraced every opportunity to experience local life; from sampling traditional dishes and fresh fruit shakes at lively night markets, enjoying spectacular sunsets over the South China Sea, and a vibrant cultural dance performance.
After an action-packed start, the group enjoyed a well-deserved rest day exploring Borneo's stunning coastline. Snorkelling, kayaking and relaxing on a local island gave students the chance to discover the region's incredible marine life before sharing a beach barbecue together.
The next stage of the expedition brought the adventure they had been preparing for – a demanding four-day trek along the Banbamgan Trail. Carrying everything they needed on their backs, the students navigated challenging jungle terrain in intense heat and humidity, crossing rope bridges, tackling muddy trails and camping beneath the stars each night. Their determination, resilience and teamwork shone through as they supported one another every step of the way.
A highlight of the expedition was the opportunity to immerse themselves in Borneo's unique natural environment. Students contributed to a rainforest conservation service project in the Kinabatangan region, gaining first-hand experience of the importance of protecting one of the world's most biodiverse ecosystems. They also visited the Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre and the Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre, deepening their understanding of wildlife conservation and the vital work being carried out to safeguard these species.
Throughout the expedition, students learned not only about Borneo's extraordinary landscapes, wildlife and culture, but also about themselves. They developed resilience in challenging conditions, strengthened their communication and leadership skills, and discovered the value of supporting one another as a team. From campfire conversations and shared moments of laughter, to overcoming physical challenges and embracing unfamiliar experiences, every day offered new opportunities for growth.
We are incredibly proud of everything our World Challenge 2026 students have achieved. Their positivity, determination and willingness to embrace every aspect of the expedition made it an unforgettable experience. The memories they have created – and the confidence, independence and friendships they have built – will stay with them for many years to come.
Congratulations to all our students for representing the School so brilliantly throughout this remarkable adventure.

pageCache.pageTitle: History of the School | Cobham Hall Independent School
pageCache.text:
1206
Norman manor house on the site of what was to become Cobham Hall is granted by King Henry II to the De Cobham family
1573
Work commences on two new Tudor wings for the house – now home to our Sixth Form Centre and Dining Rooms - after visits from Queen Elizabeth I.
1613
King James I grants the Cobham Estates to his cousin Ludovick Stuart, 2nd Duke of Lenox.
The Estates had been confiscated from the Brooke family following their involvement in a plot to put Arabella Stuart on the throne in his stead.
1625
King Charles I spends his honeymoon night at Cobham Hall.
1819
The future Queen Victoria, is born
The Duke and Duchess of Kent stay overnight at Cobham Hall. Their daughter, the future Queen Victoria, is born two weeks later.
1870
The Swiss chalet in which author Charles Dickens wrote is moved, on his death, to the grounds of Cobham Hall as a gift to his great friend, the 6th Earl of Darnley.
1882
Ivo Bligh, future 8th Earl of Darnley and captain of the England cricket team, is presented with ‘the Ashes’ on tour in Australia.
The famed urn will later rest on the mantelpiece of Cobham Hall’s Old Library for many years.
1914
Cobham Hall becomes a military hospital for the British Army and then for officers of the Australian army.
1939
Cobham Hall is used as a home for evacuees and then for RAF officers from the Battle of Britain fighter squadron based in nearby Gravesend.
1957
The 10th Earl of Darnley sells Cobham Hall to a Land Fund of the Government to preserve for the Nation.
The Hall is later sold to the Westwood Education Trust as home for a new independent school for girls.
1962
With Miss Brenda Hancock as inaugural Headmistress, Cobham Hall opens its doors to its first 50 students.
The first new independent school for girls to be opened for 16 years, Cobham Hall was the project of Mrs Bee Mansell, who wanted girls to enjoy the same public school education as provided for boys.
1966
Lady Harriet Bligh, sister of the 11th Earl of Darnley, is elected Guardian of Cobham Hall, having attended the school (housed in her own former home) since it opened.
1967
Cobham Hall joins the Round Square Conference of Schools, the first girls’ school to do so.
1971
Brooke House (currently boarding house for Sixth Form girls) is opened by Margaret Thatcher MP, who will later become Prime Minister.
1972
Miss Jill Hanson takes over as Headmistress.
She covers the swimming pool so it could be used all year round and converted the Dressmaking Room into a Physics Lab, allowing Cobham to teach Chemistry, Biology and Physics to A Level – highly unusual for a girls’ boarding school at the time.
1977
The ‘Unicorn’ Parent Teachers Association is born.
1988
Bligh House is opened by Lady Harriet Bligh.
1989
British tennis star and Wimbledon winner Virginia Wade opens the Activities Centre.
1990
English actress Susan Hampshire, three-times Emmy Award-winner and campaigner on dyslexia issues, opens the centre for learning support.
2003
The Tenison-Smith Studio Theatre is opened by former Head of Drama, Carey Tenison-Smith
2008
Cobham Hall is used as the location for the filming of box office hit ‘Wild Child’, with staff and students taking part as extras.
2012
A celebratory book is commissioned to mark the 50th anniversary of Cobham Hall, to which many Elders contribute.
2021
Mrs Wendy Barrett becomes Headmistress as Cobham Hall merges with The Mill Hill School Foundation.
2022
Cobham Hall becomes co-educational in the Sixth Form
2023
Cobham Hall announces partnership with renowned piano makers, Steinway & Sons, and takes delivery of a fine Steinway ‘B’ Grand to take pride of place in the Gilt Hall.
2024
Cobham Hall announces it will become fully co-educational from Years 7 to 13 with effect from September 2025.
2024
Opening in January 2025, Cobham Hall announces the opening of Bligh House SEND Centre located within the School site
The centre of excellence is a result of the unique collaboration between Mill Hill Education Group and Chiltern Way Academy Trust.
2025
First Lower School Boy Joined Cobham Hall!
In April 2025, Cobham welcomed Brian into Year 9 - the first boy in Lower School to join since the announcement of going fully co-educational from September 2025.
2026
Cobham Hall welcomes Mr Doug Brown as its new Headteacher
In September 2026, Cobham Hall marked the beginning of an exciting new chapter in the School’s history with the appointment of Mr Doug Brown as Headteacher.

pageCache.pageTitle: Why Choose Cobham Hall School | A Leading Independent School
pageCache.text:
Be Supported
In our caring environment and buoyed by our inclusive spirit, students are encouraged to challenge themselves. We believe that by taking part in everything Cobham Hall has to offer, our students discover more about themselves. In turn, they excel academically and leave us fully prepared for the path they have chosen. We give every child the attention they need academically, allowing each to be challenged both inside and outside of the classroom, to push themselves beyond their own personal comfort zone. Our outstanding pastoral support gives students the confidence to put themselves forward, to take a chance, to get involved, and – just as crucially – pick themselves up if things don't go as planned.“The school supports pupils in developing their confidence to pursue their goals. So they find the courage to push themselves.” ISI report 2024
Be Prepared
A Cobham Hall education is not just about results (though these are excellent) – it is an education for life, preparing today’s students for an unknown tomorrow and for jobs that have yet to be imagined. The development of essential life skills is core to the curriculum in every year group and cemented in our bespoke Perspectives course. From creativity to curiosity, communication skills to adaptability, Perspectives lessons support each child in developing the attributes and skills they will need to thrive, whatever the future brings. And in our multicultural, diverse setting, students develop the global outlook and understanding our world will need.“Pupils have an excellent understanding of the value of diversity and are well prepared for their future lives.” ISI report 2024
For a visual representation of how we integrate our values and perspectives into daily life at Cobham Hall, click here.
Be You
We believe in educating the individual. Being a small school allows us to be aware of each pupil’s talents, strengths and potential, and we encourage every student to develop all aspects of their character. As a small school, where everyone knows everyone, we have a natural advantage in providing excellent, individual care for all our students. Strong communication between Pastoral, Academic and Boarding staff ensures that each student gets the care and support needed to thrive. Our diverse student body comprises many different nationalities, backgrounds, abilities, and talents – every individual prized, valued and celebrated.
“A small, truly international school which turns out compassionate, confident and worldly-wise global citizens.” Good Schools Guide
Be Challenged
We aim to provide, and encourage students to take, as many opportunities as possible. Our outstanding co-curricular and Saturday Enrichment programmes offer a huge range of activities that provide opportunities to have fun as well as to develop or learn new skills. As a Round Square school, we offer students the chance to travel the world for conferences, exchanges and service projects. These are in addition to the day-to-day fabric of Cobham Hall, which every day offers a wealth of leadership opportunities, service activities and chances to try the new.
“A strong international focus and a huge spirit of adventure.” Muddy Stilettos
Be Inspired
Housed in a beautiful 16th century mansion surrounded by 150 acres of glorious Kent countryside, though just 30 minutes from central London, Cobham Hall’s setting is truly inspirational. Students can practise in the Downs for the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award expeditions, have campfires in the clearing where Charles Dickens’ writing chalet once stood, or enjoy BBQs in Lady Darnley’s garden. The grounds are used for enhancing classroom studies: data for environmental studies, space for physical education, and natural sets for drama, art and music are all just outside the door. Students can also enjoy life’s simpler pleasures: climbing trees, kicking a ball about, or simply relaxing in sunshine. All are activities that develop our students’ physical, social, moral and spiritual qualities, alongside the academic success that flourishes as a result.
“The building and grounds are idyllic – they are that epitome of story book British boarding school at its finest.” Muddy Stilettos

pageCache.pageTitle: Scholarships and Bursaries | Cobham Hall Independent School
pageCache.text:
Scholarships
Scholarships may be awarded to a student in recognition of exceptional ability, potential and commitment.
Students joining Cobham Hall in Years 7 to 10 can apply for a scholarship in Sport, Art, Music, or Drama. Students should apply in writing to the Headteacher.
Academic Scholarships are by invitation only. Students joining Years 7 to 10 with the potential for obtaining an Academic Scholarship are identified through Entrance Assessments and will be invited to apply for an Academic Scholarship.
Students entering Year 12 and applying for Sixth Form Scholarships must apply to the Headteacher in writing and will be required to sit a scholarship paper in a subject they intend to study. Candidates will also be interviewed by the Headteacher or another senior member of staff.
All applications made by new students will be facilitated Admissions Team.
Cobham Hall in Partnership with Steinway & Sons
Cobham Hall is excited to announce a brand-new music partnership with world-renowned Steinway & Sons and the launch of an exciting new Steinway Scholarship for talented young musicians. Read more below.Steinway & Sons Scholarship
Bursaries
The School may consider applications for a Bursary from parents of students who have passed our Entrance Assessments and been offered a full fee paying place. Bursaries are highly competitive, and the School has a limited amount of funds available each year to support these. When considering applications, results from our Entrance Assessments and scholarship applications, along with interviews and references from your child’s current school are all reviewed. A financial appraisal is also undertaken.
For further information, please contact our Admissions Team.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cobham Hall Welcomes New Head, Mr Doug Brown from September 2026
pageCache.text:
Welcoming Mr Brown as Head from September 2026
We are delighted to announce the appointment of Mr Brown as our new Head at Cobham Hall with effect from September 2026. Mr Brown will succeed Mrs Barrett, who is retiring after an extraordinary 33-year career at Cobham Hall.
Mr Brown will be joining us from Hertford Prep School, where he has been Head since 2016, bringing with him a wealth of experience in education, leadership and pastoral care. Throughout his career, he has demonstrated a strong commitment to nurturing students as individuals, creating ambitious learning environments and building supportive, inclusive school communities in which students can thrive.
CEO, Antony Spencer, commented “One of the benefits of the Mill Hill Education Group is having access to tried and tested School leaders who are already invested in the values and ethos we enjoy. To have somebody with Mr Brown’s track record taking on the leadership oof Cobham Hall is a significant coup, and the School will continue to be in very good hands.”
This appointment marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter for Cobham Hall. We are thrilled to welcome Mr Brown to our School and look forward to the energy, experience and insight he will bring to the community. He shares our belief in providing an education that enables every pupil to flourish academically, personally and socially, while fostering curiosity, confidence and a lifelong love of learning.
Mr Brown is very much looking forward to meeting our students, families and staff, and becoming part of the Cobham Hall community.
As we prepare for this transition in leadership, we extend Mr Brown a warm welcome and look forward with great optimism to the opportunities ahead as we begin this next chapter together.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding
As part of the Mill Hill Education Group, we fully recognise the importance of our moral and statutory responsibilities for safeguarding, child protection and protecting the welfare of all our pupils. The Mill Hill Education Group has pupils’ best interests at the centre of everything it does, and the Group expects all staff, volunteers, Governors, parents and pupils to share in this commitment. Safeguarding refers to measures implemented to protect the health, wellbeing and human rights of children so that they may live free from harm, abuse and neglect. We are committed to protecting every pupil from any form of abuse, whether from an adult or another pupil, and we ensure that staff, volunteers and Governors have regular training to understand and fulfil their collective responsibility in keeping our community safe and report any concerns promptly. The Group adheres to the inter-agency procedures and local protocols of the respective schools’ Local Safeguarding Children’s Partnerships (LSCPs) and Multi Agency Safeguarding Arrangements (MASAs), in line with the government guidance ‘Working Together to Safeguard Children’ and ‘Keeping Children Safe in Education’.
The Court of Governors are committed to providing and maintaining a safe and supportive culture where all staff working for Mill Hill Education Group feel confident and competent to raise any concerns regarding pupil welfare or adult behaviour towards pupils. Mill Hill Education Group is committed to instilling pupils with strong values and sense of belonging within a secure, caring and supportive learning environment, where they feel confident that adults and peers value them, will listen to them and advocate and protect them.
Cobham Hall Safeguarding Team
Our designated safeguarding team is overseen by Kelly Alleyne, Mill Hill Education Group’s Director of Safeguarding.

If you spot an issue you think should be reported to the DSL, please dial 01474 825922 to speak with Sue Carney without delay.

Cobham Hall benefits from an idyllic country setting
Our Manor House is set in 150 acres of beautiful grounds – yet enjoys excellent transport links.
Located on the edge of the Kent Downs, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, Cobham Hall is situated just off the A2, not far from Ebbsfleet International Station.
An hour by road to Stansted Airport
School Transport
Cobham Hall provides a daily minibus service for day students and weekly boarders. Our network currently extends from Blackheath to the west to Chatham in the east, and as far south as Sevenoaks. Shuttle services to local train stations at Ebbsfleet International and Gravesend may also be available.
Full details of our services and charges may be found in our transport guide:
Cobham Hall School Transport 2025 – 2026
The cost is dependent upon distance travelled. Pick-up points within 2.5 miles of Cobham Hall fall in Zone A, those 2.5 to 5 miles from the School are Zone B, while everything beyond is Zone C.
*All fees and supplemental charges quoted are inclusive of taxes, which have been added (where applicable). Fees maybe subject to change post budget – 30 October 2024 and following the imposition of VAT from January 2025.
Maps of our current routes can be found on the links below:
Blackheath – Bexleyheath – Cobham Hall
Bexley – Darenth – Longfield – Ebbsfleet – Northfleet – Cobham Hall
Sevenoaks – Otford – Orpington – Cobham Hall
Belvedere – Greenhithe – Darenth – Cobham Hall
Bromley – Sidcup – Swanley – Cobham Hall
Lewisham – Greenwich – Blackheath – Cobham Hall
Routes are reviewed annually and may be adjusted depending on demand. To find out more, please contact the School directly via enquiries@cobhamhall.com.
To book a place on one of our minibus services for a current Cobham Hall student, please complete the Minibus Request Form which can be found in the Parents’ Portal.
